name: Cumulative Radiation Dose
steps: Read the cumulative dose from the personal dosimeter display.
Record the value and the date in the check-in form.
Compare to the 600 mSv career limit: flag if above 50 % (300 mSv).
when: Once per mission day, same time each day.
mistakes: Do not confuse absorbed dose (Gy) with dose equivalent (Sv). Use the Sv reading.
escalate_if: Single-day spike above 1 mSv (ISS), 5 mSv (Lunar) or 10 mSv (Mars) — may indicate SPE.
why: Ionising radiation damages DNA and raises lifetime cancer risk. Cumulative tracking catches slow overexposure before the career limit is reached.
benefits: Early detection of elevated exposure allows mission planners to rotate crew out of high-radiation modules or activities.

actions.yellow: Review shielding options. Limit EVA time. Notify flight surgeon. Cross-check daily dose against SPE alerts.
actions.red: Mandatory ground consult. Restrict EVA. Begin radiation countermeasure protocol per NASA HRP guidelines.

note_environment: Baselines differ by environment: ISS ~100 mSv/6 mo, Lunar ~200 mSv/6 mo, Mars ~300 mSv/6 mo (transit + surface).

name: Daily Radiation Dose
equipment: TEPC or area dosimeter in crew quarters
steps: Read the 24-hour dose from the area dosimeter at the same time each day.
If the instrument shows absorbed dose (μGy), note it without converting — keep raw absorbed dose and record unit clearly.
Enter the value and check for SPE watch/warning bulletins from flight control.
when: Daily, at start of sleep period.
mistakes: Do not convert absorbed dose to dose equivalent without the correct quality factor for the environment.
escalate_if: Single-day reading is more than 3× the environment baseline — suspect Solar Particle Event.
why: Daily tracking reveals acute spikes (solar particle events) that the cumulative reading can mask.
benefits: Allows rapid crew shelter response during SPE before significant acute exposure occurs.

actions.yellow: Increase monitoring frequency. Alert flight surgeon. Cross-check with SPE forecast.
actions.red: Execute storm shelter procedure immediately. Report to mission control.

note_environment: ISS RadLab / OSDR data used for ISS baseline. If in absorbed dose only, do not convert — state so in README and use demo values for preset.

name: Blood Glucose — Fasting
steps: Fast for at least 8 hours before measuring (water is allowed).
Clean fingertip with alcohol swab; allow to air-dry. Prick the side of the fingertip.
Apply the first drop of blood to the glucometer strip; record the reading after the beep.
when: Before the first meal of the day, after at least 8 h of fasting.
mistakes: Measuring too soon after eating gives a falsely high reading. Cold extremities give falsely low readings — warm hands first.
escalate_if: Reading below 2.8 mmol/L (severe hypoglycaemia) or above 11.1 mmol/L (hyperglycaemia crisis) — act immediately.
why: Microgravity and stress alter glucose regulation. Hypoglycaemia impairs cognition and motor performance; hyperglycaemia increases infection risk.
benefits: Daily tracking catches metabolic shifts early, allowing diet or activity adjustments before clinical illness.

actions.yellow_low: Consume 15 g fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose gel). Re-test in 15 min. Report to flight surgeon.
actions.yellow_high: Review recent diet. Increase activity. Report to flight surgeon if reading persists.
actions.red_low: Administer IV/IM glucose per emergency protocol. Contact mission control immediately.
actions.red_high: Contact flight surgeon immediately. Begin medical assessment protocol.

source_tag: NASA-STD-3001 Vol.1 §4.9; WHO glucose reference ranges

name: Blood Glucose — Post-meal
steps: Measure exactly 2 hours after the start of a main meal.
Record the meal type (normal, high-carb, emergency ration).
Apply blood to strip and record the reading.
when: 2 hours after main meal, at least twice per week.
mistakes: Starting the timer at the end of the meal, not the start, inflates the result.
escalate_if: Reading above 11.1 mmol/L at 2 h post-meal on two consecutive days.
why: Post-meal spikes predict impaired glucose tolerance and long-term metabolic risk during extended missions.
benefits: Allows mission dietitians to adjust meal carbohydrate composition and timing to keep glucose within safe bounds.

actions.yellow: Flag to flight surgeon. Review meal composition. Increase post-meal activity (10-min walk equivalent).
actions.red: Ground consult required. Begin enhanced metabolic monitoring protocol.

source_tag: NASA-STD-3001 Vol.1 §4.9; ADA Standards of Medical Care 2024
